newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity eases in thin demand.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity eases in thin demand.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) eased Tuesday in thin demand with mild temperatures through the state, industry sources said.
Lower spot Texas natural gas prices put downward pressure on next-day ERCOT power prices, the sources said.
Temperatures through Texas were expected to be in the high 70s and low 80s degrees Fahrenheit range on Wednesday.
"There is not any demand at all," said one ERCOT marketer, who said next-day trade in the state was thin.
Texas spot gas was said to have eased Tuesday by about 20 cents to near $3.00 per million British thermal units.
ERCOT firm, peak power for Wednesday delivery was pegged at $29.00-31.00 from $33.00-34.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Non-firm peak ERCOT was notionally said to be talked at a significant discount to firm, near $22.00-23.00, with the low demand.
Firm off-peak ERCOT power transactions were pegged steady at $11.00-14.00, the sources said.
ERCOT January/February peak power prices eased to $29.75-30.25 from $30.50-31.00 on Monday, the sources said.
